function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Out of policy calls (20/20) with the block not verifiably inside the bowl. I localised the block and straddled it three times, but every close measured 0.016-0.033 (jaws on empty air) or 0.221 followed by a slip-out during the lift, so the block was never carried. My last move was a low wedge-push that slid the block about 6 cm toward the bowl; the fixed front view now shows it at the near rim while the side view still shows it resting on the table outside the bowl. I cannot claim success, so I am reporting failure.", "hindsight": "Camera axes measured by deliberate parallax: in the wrist view image-right is world -y (verified twice, +46 mm and -101 mm of y motion moved both landmarks ~44 px and ~93 px exactly as predicted), and the wrist camera is pitched about 40 deg toward +x, so image-up is roughly +x and anything directly below the eef projects to up-coordinate -tan(40)=-0.84, which is exactly where the finger pads sit, i.e. the pads hang essentially directly under eef_pos. The eef-to-fingertip offset is small, about 15-20 mm, not the 50 mm of a real Panda: at eef z=0.870 the pads were still above a 50 mm block whose top is at z=0.85, so you must reach about eef z=0.83-0.845 to get the jaws alongside the block (z=0.80 is the table). The 20-call budget, not the 900 steps, is the binding constraint: a move_to with no gripper delta executes only 2-5 control steps, so commanded targets are barely reached; commanding an intermediate gripper value such as 0.5 keeps the current open/closed latch (0.35 and 0.65 thresholds) while giving the interpolator a large delta, which bought 38-80 steps per call. The side camera is NOT fixed, the bowl and block both drifted about 45 px vertically between observations, so use it only for coarse relative cues; the front camera is genuinely fixed (block and bowl pixel positions identical over 800 steps), its horizontal is world y, larger x appears lower in the image, and its scale is about 2.5 mm/px at table height. Grasp recipe: read the block offset from the pad-gap centre in the wrist view (about 0.6-1 mm/px), translate to centre it in y, descend to eef z=0.83, close in a separate call, then lift gently, because a shallow grip that only catches the block top will shake loose in transit. Yaw stays near 0 and the jaws separate along world y, so centring in y matters far more than in x, where roughly 20 mm overlap with the pads is enough. Finally, the bowl contains a small fixed red marker dot visible from above; do not mistake it for the target block."}
